narrative.title: The Airport Gate Directory
narrative.scenario: An airport builds a type-ahead directory for gate labels: staff type a label fragment and the kiosk must confirm whether a full label exists, or whether any label begins with that fragment. The directory is rebuilt per shift, so it needs fast insert, exact lookup, and prefix lookup — all sharing one letter-by-letter structure.
narrative.inputFormat: A list of operations, each either ["insert", word], ["search", word], or ["startsWith", prefix]. The first operation is always ["Trie"].
narrative.outputFormat: Return one entry per search or startsWith operation: true or false. insert yields null.
constraints: words and prefixes use lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: "apple" is stored exactly; "app" only becomes a full label after its own insert.
The prefix "ga" matches, but "ga" alone is not a stored label.

hintLevels: Level 1: Each node holds 26 child slots and a flag that says a word ends here.
Level 2: Walk letters down the tree; insert creates missing nodes, search additionally checks the end flag.
Level 3: startsWith is search without the end-flag requirement — factor the walk into a shared helper.
